scenarios.title: The Pregnancy
scenarios.text: {love_interest} is pregnant, and the due date falls right in the middle of the season. You're thrilled, and already counting weeks on the schedule.

choices.label: Plan to be there
choices.result: You tell {coach} now that you'll miss a game if the baby comes on a Sunday. The coach says it's the right call and means it.

choices.label: Make a plan with everyone
choices.result: You make a plan with {love_interest}, the coach and both families: who's on call, which flights, which bags. It feels like a playbook, and it helps.

choices.label: Hope for the bye week
choices.result: You hope the baby comes in the bye week. You also keep a bag packed in the car and check your phone at every break.

scenarios.title: The Baby's First Year
scenarios.text: Sleepless nights with a newborn during the season.

choices.label: Take the night shifts
choices.result: You take the night shifts on off days. You're tired and close.

choices.label: Sleep in shifts
choices.result: You and {love_interest} sleep in shifts by the schedule. It works, roughly.

choices.label: Ask for help
choices.result: You ask the grandparents to come for a month. Everyone sleeps.

scenarios.title: The Daycare
scenarios.text: Finding daycare in a city where you might not live next year.

choices.label: Do the research
choices.result: You visit six places and pick the best one.

choices.label: Ask the team families
choices.result: You ask the other team families. They have a list and a group chat.

choices.label: Hire a nanny for now
choices.result: You hire a nanny for the season and decide later.

scenarios.title: The In-Laws
scenarios.text: {love_interest}'s family visits for two weeks during the season.

choices.label: Be the host
choices.result: You make them feel welcome every evening. {love_interest} notices.

choices.label: Keep your routine
choices.result: You keep your routine and see them at dinner.

choices.label: Plan their days
choices.result: You plan their days so everyone has something to do.

scenarios.title: The Kicking Video Series
scenarios.text: You start a video series teaching kids how to kick.

choices.label: Make it good
choices.result: You make it good: real drills, real mistakes, real fixes.

choices.label: Bring in {holder}
choices.result: You bring {holder} in for an episode. It's the most popular one.

choices.label: Keep it simple
choices.result: You film one video a month on your phone.

scenarios.title: The Podcast Guest Spot
scenarios.text: A popular podcast wants you as a weekly guest. The host likes controversy and has a reputation for getting athletes to say things about their teammates.

choices.label: Set your terms first
choices.result: Terms, agreed up front: no teammates, no coaches, no locker room. It's good radio anyway, and the host respects the line.

choices.label: Say yes and wing it
choices.result: Yes, and you're great at it, until the fourth episode, when you say too much about a teammate. You apologize to him in person.

choices.label: Pass on the podcast
choices.result: No podcast this year. The host finds another kicker, who says something he regrets by October, and you're quietly relieved.

scenarios.title: The Teammate Who Becomes a Friend
scenarios.text: A teammate has become your closest friend in the league: same humor, same bad taste in movies, families who get along. You realize it on a road trip, laughing at three in the morning.

choices.label: Make time for it
choices.result: Time, made on purpose: dinners, families, the off days together. The friendship becomes the best part of the whole job.

choices.label: Train together all summer
choices.result: A whole summer of training together, every morning. You both get better, and the friendship gets a rhythm of its own.

choices.label: Keep it easy
choices.result: No effort required, and none spent. Some friendships don't need any work at all, and this one never does, even years later.

scenarios.title: The Holder's Wedding
scenarios.text: {holder} asks you to be in the wedding party. It's in June, in {holder}'s hometown, and there's a rehearsal dinner where you're expected to say something.

choices.label: Say yes and give a toast
choices.result: Yes, and a toast at the rehearsal dinner that nobody forgets: the first hold, the bad haircut, the night they saved your season.

choices.label: Organize the weekend
choices.result: The whole weekend, organized by you: the hotel block, the shuttle, the backup suits. {holder} doesn't lift a finger and cries about it.

choices.label: Show up and enjoy it
choices.result: Showing up, standing where they tell you, dancing badly at the reception. You enjoy every minute, and {holder} says it was perfect.

scenarios.title: The Fan Club
scenarios.text: Fans start an official fan club in your name, with T-shirts and a newsletter. They want you at the first meeting, in the back room of a pizza place on a Tuesday.

choices.label: Go to the meeting
choices.result: Two hours in the back room of the pizza place. They make you an honorary member, and the T-shirt becomes your favorite shirt.

choices.label: Send a message and a ball
choices.result: A recorded message and a signed ball for the raffle. They play the message three times and frame the ball.

choices.label: Thank them online
choices.result: A thank-you post, and your Tuesday stays your own. The club grows anyway, without you, which feels a little strange and kind of nice.

scenarios.title: The Rival's Big Contract
scenarios.text: {tyler} signs a bigger contract than yours, by a lot, and the media want a comment. A reporter reads you the number, slowly, and waits.

choices.label: Congratulate him
choices.result: Congratulations, publicly, and you mean it. He texts you thanks within the hour and a photo of the two of you at seventeen.

choices.label: Decline to comment
choices.result: No comment, politely, and you walk away from the cameras. It makes a headline anyway: 'Kicker silent on rival's huge new deal.'

choices.label: Keep the number private
choices.result: The number, written on a card, goes inside your locker where only you can see it. Every practice that month has a little more in it.

scenarios.title: The Charity Golf Tournament
scenarios.text: You host your own charity golf tournament for the first time: thirty-six foursomes, a silent auction, and a sponsor who keeps asking for 'more visibility'.

choices.label: Run it yourself
choices.result: Every detail, run by you, from the sign-up sheet to the last trophy. You're exhausted, and the tournament raises twice the goal.

choices.label: Invite the old college crew
choices.result: Your college teammates, invited, and {best_friend} runs the auction. It turns into a reunion, and the bidding gets very competitive.

choices.label: Find a sponsor to run it
choices.result: A sponsor who covers everything and handles the details. It raises more than you'd have alone, and feels less like yours.

scenarios.title: The Investment Club
scenarios.text: A group of teammates forms an investment club: monthly meetings, a shared account, a lot of opinions about technology stocks. They want you in, and the first meeting is at the quarterback's house.

choices.label: Join the club
choices.result: Joined. The meetings are mostly jokes and some good ideas, and the account does fine, and the friendships do better.

choices.label: Join with limits
choices.result: In, with a small amount and one rule: nothing you don't understand. You end up explaining index funds to a linebacker, who becomes your biggest convert.

choices.label: Keep money and friends apart
choices.result: Money and friends don't mix, for you. You stay out, politely, and still go to the meetings for the food.

scenarios.title: The Second Car
scenarios.text: You buy a second car, and then realize you never drive the first one.

choices.label: Sell one
choices.result: You sell one and feel smarter for it.

choices.label: Give one to {sibling}
choices.result: You give the old one to {sibling}. He cries a little.

choices.label: Keep both
choices.result: You keep both. They sit in the driveway, shining.
